title: Who starts and stops the client
about: A reload in development: the provider starts the client, React's StrictMode stops it, and the provider starts it again.

stops.say: The page loads and React mounts the auth provider. ConvexAuthProvider built the client; this provider, inside it, is the one that starts it.
The client starts. First it listens for changes from other tabs, then it reports that it is loading.

checks.say: It listens for changes from other tabs.
It reports that it is loading.

stops.say: It reads the session from storage: both keys, once. Memory does not take what it read yet: that waits for the reads to come back.
React's StrictMode unmounts the provider on purpose (in development only). The provider stops the client it started, and the client stops listening to other tabs.
From here until the client listens again, nothing is listening. A change made in another tab now would be missed, and memory would drift from storage. This gap is where the drift bugs live.
The provider starts the same client again. This time the client only listens again: it does not start over, and it does not read storage a second time.

checks.say: It listens for changes from other tabs again.
No storage read was reported in this start.

stops.say: Only now does the first start finish: memory takes what it read, and the client stops loading. Memory agrees with storage: signed in or signed out, as storage said. The list shows this line under the first start, where it belongs, though it came last.

checks.say: It belongs to the first start.

stops.say: On main, whoever mounts the provider starts and stops the client. The change under review moves that to whoever creates the client.
